q1_issues.issue: The complement of 'agree' is sealed as a term argument, but sealing is licensed only for finite clausal attitude complements, embedded questions, imperatives, counterfactuals and strength-0 denials — a matrix verb with a non-finite complement reifies that eventuality at top level under Theme instead.
The sealed complement carries only its event class, with no Agent or any other role, so nothing in the parse records who was to come.

q2_gaps: verbless expressive speech-act formula ('Thanks', 'Sorry', 'Congratulations') — the instruction set routes declaratives, questions and imperatives, but nothing says whether such a formula is asserted as an occurring event, and this parse asserts a thank event with no participants and no tense

subject-control infinitival complement ('agree to V', 'promise to V', 'refuse to V') — only causatives, aspectual inceptives, purpose infinitives and degree-governed infinitives are covered, so nothing states whether the complement is sealed or reified at top level, or whether the controller's role is copied into it
gerund clause as the object of a preposition — the oblique rule says the object NP follows ordinary NP rules, which do not cover a clausal object
notes: The (For <event> …) oblique is correctly chosen over Beneficiary, since the agreeing is the ground of the thanking rather than a benefited party. Most of what is missing is forced by the ellipsis (no speaker or addressee is in the text, and the instruction set forbids minting them).
